frame_e7971f446cb4.question: Vulnerability analysis of Vault
artifact_refs: Access control and privileged state transitions
Accounting invariants between assets, shares, deposits, and claims
Interactions with strategy and external token transfers

history.rationale: WHY NOW: Vault is the central custody and accounting component, governing deposits, withdrawals, yield claims, strategies, and share issuance; defects here can directly affect all user funds and permissions. EXIT CRITERIA: Review the complete Vault state model and every externally reachable state transition, verify authorization and reentrancy assumptions, trace token/share accounting across normal and emergency flows, and document any exploitable invariant violations or conclude that no material vulnerability is supported by the code.

frame_ea8850407ea2.question: Vulnerability analysis of SandclockFactory
artifact_refs: CREATE2 salt and init-code handling across deployment entrypoints
Deployment address predictability, collision behavior, and code-existence checks
Caller-supplied contract creation code and resulting privilege assumptions

history.rationale: WHY NOW: SandclockFactory is an unvisited major permission and deployment component, and its trust-gated CREATE2 flows can affect the integrity of every deployed Vault and DCA instance. The graph notes constructor trust assumptions, caller-supplied init code, and deployment rejection checks, making authorization bypass, deterministic-address collisions, or malicious implementation deployment important to assess before revisiting already completed components. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace constructor trust initialization and every public deployment path, verify authorization cannot be bypassed, confirm CREATE2 salts and init code cannot cause unsafe collisions or substitute unintended bytecode, and establish that successful deployments always produce the intended contract type with no exploitable post-deployment trust or ownership configuration.
